title: Startup scripts, metadata and the instance service account

videos.script: A new machine knows nothing about your shop. This lesson is about how it finds out, and about the identity it acts with. {{script}} First, the startup script. You hand it to Compute Engine as metadata. The machine runs it as root on every boot, not just the first. So it has to be safe to run twice. {{server}} Then the metadata server, at one address inside every machine. It answers questions about the machine itself. And it insists on one header, to stop a whole class of attack. {{identity}} Then the identity. A service account attached to the machine gives your code a token that lasts an hour. No key file ever touches the disk. {{scopes}} Last, the two checks every call meets. The token's scope, and the account's roles. Both have to say yes, and only one of them is worth tuning.
